privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What data SagaShelf stores, what it is used for and what your rights are.
privacy.intro: SagaShelf is a personal, non-commercial project to search and track anime, movies, series, books and manga. This policy explains what data we store and what you can do with it.

who.title: Who is responsible
who.body: SagaShelf is run by its creator as a personal project. For any question about your data, write to {{email}}.

data.title: What data we store
data.intro: We store only what is needed for your account and your library to work:
data.account: Account: your email, your username and, if you use a password, a protected version of it. Clerk manages the password and SagaShelf never stores it.
data.google: Google sign-in: if you choose it, Google shares your email, name and profile photo with Clerk. We do not access anything else in your Google account.
data.profile: Profile: your display name, bio, language, privacy level and the photo you choose. Before a photo is sent, your browser crops and shrinks it, which also removes data the file may carry, such as the place where it was taken.
data.library: Library: for each title you save, its status, your progress, your score, the dates you started and finished it, how many times you watched it again, your notes and a visibility level (private by default). If you change the level of an entry, the people that level allows will see it (see "Who sees your profile"). Nobody else sees your notes.
data.favorites: Site favorites: entries with public visibility from people with a public profile count, without a name, in the Trending lists, and a title only appears when at least 3 people share it. If you change an entry's visibility, your profile level or delete your account, you stop counting within an hour.
data.viewings: Viewing history: the dates and notes of each time you watched a title, if you choose to record them.
data.contact: Contact messages: what you write on the contact page (the kind of message, the text and, if you were not signed in and want a reply, the email you leave) is kept to handle it, is seen only by whoever runs the site and is deleted after 90 days. If you sent it with your account, it is also deleted when you delete your account and is in your data export.
data.technical: Technical data: when you visit the site, the hosting provider records request data (such as the IP address, the requested page and the browser) to run and protect the service.
data.analytics: Usage statistics: we measure how the site is used with our own system, with no cookies and without storing your IP address or your account. The details are in <stats>“Usage statistics”</stats>.
data.social: Relationships: whom you follow, whom you blocked and whom you muted, and the follow requests you send and receive. The person you mute does not know.
data.reports: Reports and pictures: the reports you send, and for each picture you try to upload, the date, a fingerprint of the file (not the image), the result of the check and your IP address. We do not tell the person you report that it was you.

stats.title: Usage statistics
stats.intro: To know how SagaShelf is used, we measure visits with our own system. It uses no cookies, stores nothing in your browser and uses no third-party service: the data is kept in our own database. This is what is measured:
stats.pages: The pages you open, as a kind of page (for example “a person's profile” or “a title page”), not with the name of the person or of the title.
stats.source: Where you come from: a search engine, a social network or another site (only its main address, not the exact page), and the campaign tags in the address, such as utm_source, if it has them.
stats.time: How long each page was visible.
stats.speed: How fast each page loads and responds: how long its main content takes to appear, how much it moves while it loads and how long it takes to answer a click or a tap. The movement and response measures cover your whole visit, and all of them are counted for the page your visit started on.
stats.search: The type of each search (for example anime or books), never the text you type.
stats.steps: When you add a title to your library and when you follow a person, without keeping which title or whom.
stats.place: Your country and region (not your city), which Cloudflare tells us, and whether you use a phone or a computer.
stats.notStored: We do not store your IP address, your account, your name, your email, the text of your searches, or which exact title you view or whom you follow: none of this is linked to your visits.
stats.visitor: To count one person once in a day, we work out a code from your IP address and your browser, mixed with a random value that changes every day and that we keep only for today and yesterday. We store the code and not the IP address; since the value changes every day, the code cannot be used to recognize you from one day to the next.
stats.optOut: If your browser sends the “Do Not Track” signal or Global Privacy Control (GPC), we measure nothing about your visit.
stats.keep: The events of each visit are kept for 13 months and then deleted. Before that they are summarized in totals per day (for example, how many visits a page had), which no longer carry any visitor code and are kept with no time limit.

not.title: What we do not do
not.body: We do not sell your data, we do not show ads, and we do not use tracking cookies.

processors.title: Who it is shared with
processors.intro: We use these providers to run the service:
processors.clerk: Clerk: manages accounts and sign-in, and hosts profile pictures. When you see a picture, your browser connects to Clerk, which receives your IP address, even if you do not have an account.
processors.neon: Neon: hosts the database where your profile and the usage statistics are stored.
processors.cloudflare: Cloudflare: hosts the site, delivers the pages, protects it against abuse, tells us the country and region of each visit, and keeps a temporary copy of searches and covers for up to one day, not linked to your account. It also stores the encrypted backup copies of the database.
processors.github: GitHub: runs the daily job that creates the encrypted backup copies. The copies are not stored on GitHub.
processors.sightengine: Sightengine: checks each profile picture you upload, before it is saved, to detect sexual content. It receives only the image, not your name, your email or your account. According to Sightengine, it deletes the image after processing it, and it may process it in the European Union, Canada or the United States.
processors.titles: Title data sources (TMDB, Open Library and MangaDex): when you search or open a title, our servers send them the search text or the title's identifier to get its data. They do not receive your name, email, account or cookies. Covers are loaded through our server, so those sources do not see who visits the site.
processors.outro: These providers may process data outside Mexico, including in the United States. We use them only to run the service.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use only necessary cookies: one that remembers your language, one that remembers whether you prefer light or dark mode, one that remembers how you like to see your library (covers, titles only or grid), and Clerk's session cookies, which keep you signed in. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: We keep your data while your account exists. If you delete your account, we erase your profile, username, email and everything you created (your library with its notes and viewing history, and your follows, follow requests, blocks and mutes), and Clerk deletes your sign-in data. Only an internal record with no personal data remains, so the account cannot be reactivated by mistake. There are two exceptions, to look into abuse: the record of each picture you tried to upload is kept for 90 days, even if you delete your account, and reports are kept even if the account of the reporter or of the reported person is deleted, including the address of the reported picture. Server logs are kept for a limited time. We also keep encrypted backup copies of the database for up to 30 days, and the database provider may keep its own copies for a short period. If you delete your account, your data may remain in those copies until they expire.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: In your settings you can download a copy of your data (including your library), import it back, change your profile and delete your account. For any other request (access, correction or objection to the use of your data, the ARCO rights and their equivalents in other laws) write to {{email}}.

age.title: Minors
age.body: SagaShelf is not aimed at children under 13. If you think a minor created an account, write to us and we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If what we store or who we share it with changes, we will update this page and its date.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Write to us at {{email}} or use the contact page, linked at the foot of every page.

profile.title: Who sees your profile
profile.intro: Your profile is at a public address (/u/ and your username) that search engines do not index. What it shows depends on the privacy level you choose in your settings:
profile.public: Public: anyone, signed in or not, sees your username, your name, your picture, your bio, how many people follow you, how many you follow and how many are your friends, and the entries of your library that you marked as visible to everyone. Anyone signed in can also find you by your username on the Social page.
profile.friends: Private: anyone you have not blocked sees only your username, your name and your picture, and can send you a request to follow you. Anyone signed in can also find you by your username on the Social page. Your bio, your counts and your library are seen only by your friends (people who follow you and whom you follow). If you accept a request, that person follows you, but does not see your content until you follow them too; you can do that when you accept, and if their profile is also private, they have to accept your request.
profile.private: Total privacy: nobody but you sees your profile, not even that it exists, nobody can find you in the search and nobody can send you requests.
profile.rules: Each entry of your library has its own level, and the stricter of the entry and your profile applies. Nobody sees your notes. The people who follow you appear in your list of followers according to the level of their own profile. If you block someone, or they block you, they stop seeing and finding your profile and you stop seeing and finding theirs, and the follows between you are removed.
profile.requests: We keep the follow requests you send and receive until they are answered, cancelled, one of you blocks the other or one of the accounts is deleted. If you decline a request nobody is told: we keep it as declined, and to the person who sent it, it still looks sent until they cancel it. It is part of the copy of your data that you can download.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By creating an account or using SagaShelf you accept these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the service.

service.title: The service
service.body: SagaShelf is a personal, non-commercial project. It is offered as is, with no guarantee that it is always available, and it may change or stop working at any time.

account.title: Your account
account.body: You are responsible for the activity of your account and for keeping your access safe. You must be at least 13 years old, give us true information and have only one account.

use.title: Acceptable use
use.harass: harass, threaten or discriminate against other people;
use.spam: send spam or post misleading content;
use.piracy: share links to pirated or illegal content;
use.abuse: try to get into accounts or systems without permission, or overload the service;
use.impersonate: pretend to be someone else, or choose a username that impersonates them.
use.stalk: follow, or send follow requests to, other people in bulk or insistently, or look for someone who has blocked you;

content.title: Your content
content.body: You are responsible for what you write in your profile (name, bio and photo) and in your library (for example, your notes). You choose who sees it with your privacy level (see the Privacy Policy); the notes in your library are seen by no one else. You keep your rights over your content and allow us to store it and show it in the service according to that choice. If you import a file, it must contain only your own data.

titles.title: Title data
titles.body: Information about movies, series, anime, books and manga comes from third parties and is not ours (see the <credits>Credits</credits>). It may contain errors or change, and we do not guarantee that it is accurate or complete.

suspension.title: Suspension
suspension.body: We may suspend or delete accounts that break these terms or put the service at risk.

liability.title: Limitation of liability
liability.body: To the extent the law allows, SagaShelf and its creator are not responsible for losses that result from using the service or from it being unavailable.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.body: We may update these terms. When we do, we will change the date of this page.

people.title: Other people
people.body: You can follow other people, block them and mute them. Blocking hides your profile from that person and theirs from you, and removes the follows between you. We limit how many people you can follow per hour to prevent spam. If a person locks their profile or makes it private, respect their decision.
